To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the evolution of antibiotic resistance is a complex process that involves the simultaneous acquisition of mutations with different functions, and that these mutations generate cross-resistance to many other drugs.

(1) cross-resistance between antibiotics is a common phenomenon in bacteria, (2) the molecular basis of cross-resistance is largely driven by convergent evolution, (3) the cross-resistance interaction map can be predicted based on chemogenomic similarity between drugs, and (4) the cross-resistant mutants have reduced fitness in the absence of antibiotics, indicating the possibility of using these mutants as a novel strategy to combat antimicrobial resistance.
